This Custom Sprinter Van Conversion Is a Luxurious Wellness Clinic on Wheels
23 photos
Photo: Vancini Conversions
Panel and cargo vans have proved their versatility time and time again. Apart from mobile living spaces, lately they have become a popular alternative to traditional business premises as well, offering the freedom to take a service directly to customers.
There are plenty of thriving mobile businesses that are operated out of a meticulously converted vehicle, from retail shops to healthcare clinics and specialized service businesses. Just like in the case of conventional camper vans, the possibilities are endless when it comes to transforming a van into a mobile workspace, but they are largely determined by the nature of the business and the creativity behind the conversion.
For their latest build, Vancini Conversions put their extensive expertise to work to create a mobile wellness clinic like no other. Designed and built for Calyx Drip, this custom van conversion is far from a basic mobile business; it’a a van built with intention.
Calyx Drip offers mobile IV therapy and medical-grade wellness services, and they needed a space that exudes warmth, calm, and professionalism; a space where clients can relax and rest assured they get professional, personalized care.
The idea was to add versatility to their operations, allowing them to provide their services on the go. With this mobile clinic, they can reach customers wherever they are.
Photo: Vancini Conversions Built inside a 2026 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170-inch wheelbase, this mobile clinic features a custom layout, specialized equipment, and carefully selected finishes that create a distinctly luxurious atmosphere inside. With custom leather reclining chairs, elegant curved LED lighting, and warm colors, the clinic will deliver wellness services in a setting that feels more like a high-end spa than a vehicle.
The base vehicle is a rear-wheel-drive Sprinter van powered by a 2.0-liter four-cylinder twin-turbo engine paired with a nine-speed automatic transmission. On the outside, it’s finished in elegant black with a full-custom branded wrap by Branded Wraps, which advertises the vehicle’s identity from a distance.
The team at Vancini Conversions equipped it with a 13.1-foot (4-meter) Fiamma F45S awning for some shaded space outside, as well as Atlas Roadcamp side and rear steps for easy entry. On top of the van, a Flatline Van Company roof rack holds 400 watts of solar panels, a Nomadic Cooling X3 12V air-conditioning unit, and a black Maxxair 7500K roof fan. The van also features some small AMA acrylic windows that can be opened from inside.
Photo: Vancini Conversions But what truly makes this van conversion stand out is its luxurious interior. The priorities of the van outfitter were quite different from when creating a mobile living space, but their craftsmanship and attention to detail still prevail. They leveraged the available square footage inside to create a functional space where the folks at Calyx Drip can provide quality services.
For a cozy, secure feel, the van has a closed-cab configuration, with a partition wall built by Vancini separating the driver’s area from the clinic. On that wall, they mounted a 55-inch LG 4K OLED TV, with access to it from the cab in case they need to replace it in the future.
The actual clinic space in the back is fitted with custom-stitched IV clinic chairs, long cabinets along each side of the van, and a rear bathroom. The arrangement is thought out to optimize efficiency and make tasks easy to perform.
Photo: Vancini Conversions The client wanted a warm ambiance inside, and Vancini created just that with a cohesive color scheme of light creams and wood tones, combined with durable, premium materials. The walls are made from flexible wood, finished with several coats of Italian limewash paint and a protective coating, giving the interior an upscale look, the cabinets are made from Baltic birch core laminated wood, and underfoot, they used stone-effect Lonseal flooring.
The gently curved ceiling incorporates recessed lighting, and Corian countertops add another elegant touch. Oatmeal-colored Marathon tweed upholstery was used around the rear door pillars, while brushed-gold accents can be observed on the custom-made Calyx Drip sign at the front, the baseboards, handles, sink, and faucet.
The client seats are custom-made reclining chairs from Premier Products, and though they have seatbelts, they are not meant to be used while the van is in motion. They are only meant for clients to settle in during their treatments. They are custom upholstered and feature the company’s logo stitched in.
Photo: Vancini Conversions Another nice detail is the custom CNC-cut, backlit logo on the passenger-side wall, which Vancini says it was designed in collaboration with Overland Interiors and was a very labor-intensive project.
The cabinets behind the client chairs are meant to keep specialized equipment and supplies organized, and a Vitrifrigo C51 refrigerator is also included. One of the cabinets has various drawers and open cubbies, and the other houses the components of the electrical system.
Photo: Vancini Conversions The day-to-day operations will be supported by a 920Ah heated Blizzard lithium battery bank, paired with a Victron MultiPlus-II 12/3000 inverter-charger, an Orion 50A DC-DC charger, a Victron 100/30 solar charge controller, and a Cerbo GX MK2 monitoring system with a GX Touch 70 display. Apart from the vehicle's alternator and rooftop solar panels, the batteries can also be charged via a 30-amp shore power connection.
A solid door leads to the rear bathroom, which is fitted with a Laveo Dryflush toilet, an overhead cabinet, a sink and faucet integrated into a custom-designed plumbing system. The van is also equipped with a 4kW Eberspächer diesel heater for a comfortable temperature inside.
